title: CNET's Article-Writing AI Is Already Publishing Very Dumb Errors
supports_claim: Futurism documented three specific errors in one CNET AI-generated finance explainer; after contact CNET corrected the article and a correction described a fourth error.
limitations: Secondary reporting on one inspected article; it does not establish an error rate across every CNET AI-assisted article or prove reader financial loss.

title: CNET's AI Journalist Appears to Have Committed Extensive Plagiarism
supports_claim: Futurism presented side-by-side examples of structural and wording similarities between CNET AI-written articles and earlier articles from other publishers without attribution.
limitations: The source reports an investigation and an expert opinion about plagiarism; it is not a court or regulator finding and the underlying generation mechanism was not independently audited.

title: Sci-fi publisher Clarkesworld halts pitches amid deluge of AI-generated stories
supports_claim: The Guardian reported that Clarkesworld closed submissions after its editor said rejections and bans for suspected AI-generated or plagiarized submissions rose from about 10 in a typical month to 100 in January and more than 500 by 21 February 2023.
limitations: Counts and AI attribution come from the founding editor; the article notes detectors were unreliable and provides no independent classification audit.

title: I Would Rather See My Books Get Pirated Than This (Or: Why Goodreads and Amazon Are Becoming Dumpster Fires)
supports_claim: Jane Friedman documented five unauthorized book titles credited to her and later updated that the titles had been removed from Amazon and Goodreads; she explained why she believed they were AI-generated.
limitations: First-person account by the affected author; AI generation was her informed belief rather than a disclosed provenance record or independent technical finding.

title: Amazon removes books 'generated by AI' for sale under author's name
supports_claim: The Guardian independently reported that five books falsely listed as written by Jane Friedman were removed and clearly attributed the AI-generation claim to Friedman's belief.
limitations: The seller and generation process were not identified; no sales figures or measured downstream financial harm were reported.

title: Self-publishers must declare if content sold on Amazon's site is AI-generated
supports_claim: The Guardian reported Amazon's later KDP requirement that publishers disclose AI-generated content and its distinction between AI-generated and AI-assisted content.
limitations: Reports a platform policy after the Friedman incident; Amazon did not disclose enforcement performance or whether buyers would see the declaration.

title: Copyright Registration Guidance: Works Containing Material Generated by Artificial Intelligence
supports_claim: The U.S. Copyright Office states that copyright protects human-authored expression and that registration applicants must disclose AI-generated material and explain the human contribution.
limitations: Official U.S. registration guidance only; it does not decide infringement or authorship rules in Vietnam or the European Union and applies case by case.

title: Luật số 71/2025/QH15 của Quốc hội: Luật Công nghiệp công nghệ số
publisher: Cơ sở dữ liệu quốc gia về văn bản pháp luật
supports_claim: Vietnam's Digital Technology Industry Law defines AI-system roles and risk categories; Articles 41 to 45 require human control and transparency and require notice when an AI system directly interacts with users.
limitations: Framework law effective 1 January 2026; the precise product-output identification list and sector-specific implementation must be confirmed by Vietnamese counsel for the scoped pilot.

title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence
publisher: Official Journal of the European Union
supports_claim: EU AI Act Article 50 requires notice for direct AI interaction and machine-readable marking for generative outputs; deployers publishing AI text on public-interest matters must disclose it unless the stated human-review and editorial-responsibility exception applies.
limitations: Classification and role allocation depend on the concrete product architecture and use; other EU law such as data protection and copyright remains outside this single-source assessment.

title: Transparency obligations under Article 50 of the AI Act
supports_claim: The European Commission explains provider and deployer roles and confirms that Article 50 transparency duties apply from 2 August 2026 with a limited marking grace period only for qualifying pre-existing systems.
limitations: Commission implementation guidance is authoritative but does not replace a product-specific legal assessment or a national authority or court decision.
